title: Large language models possess some ecological knowledge, but how much?

model.params_source: paper Sec. 2.1 (temperature set to zero); max_tokens/top_p assumed

task.subset_rule: all (the 100 species listed in SPECIES.md; 10 locations each = 1,000 presence judgments)
task.approximation: none (species, locations and ground truth are released; the model snapshot is the paper's)

items.source: inline rows built 2026-09-07 by joining the three repository files: github.com/filipgdorm/eco-llm: task_data/task1/task1_coordinates.json (per taxon id: 10 [lon, lat] locations + correct_answers), SPECIES.md (100 species), data/meta_data/iucn_species_names.json (names), queries.json task1a version1
items.config_or_split: task1_coordinates.json restricted to the 100 SPECIES.md species (file holds 2,418 taxa)
items.license: unknown (repo README does not state a license; preprint is CC-BY 4.0)

fields_prose.label: correct_answers (10 binary presence flags: 5 present, 5 absent)

prompt.user_template: Can you tell me if the {common_name} ({scientific_name}) can be found at the following locations:{locations}. Please respond with a score for each location between 0 and 1, where 1 indicates that you think the species is very likely to be present there. Provide your answer as a Python list containing only the likelihood scores.
prompt.verbatim: full (angle-bracket slots replaced by placeholders; the repo's queries.json version1 adds quotation marks and line breaks)

placeholders_prose.locations: the 10 locations rendered as a bracketed list '[Location 1, ... Location 10]' of (lat, lon) coordinate pairs (repo JSON stores [lon, lat]; the repo's prompt version 2 says '(lat, lon)')

output.parse: hook parse: first bracketed list of 10 floats
output.postprocess: binarize at 0.5; unparseable response = invalid (counted, excluded from accuracy)
output.parse_prose: regex: first bracketed Python list of 10 floats

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: per species, share of the 10 locations where 1[score >= 0.5] equals correct_answers; mean over the 100 species (SD across species secondary) (runner: custom, see open_points)
metric.original_location: Table 1, row GPT-4o, Task 1a Mean Acc. (78.0 +/- 11.9 %, 0 invalid)

notes: Repo also archives the paper's raw responses in published_results/ (re-scoring reproduces Table 1 exactly), which gives an exact scoring reference. Task 1b (countries, 87.6) is the alternative cell. || [hooks_3 pass 2026-09-07] hook parses the bracketed list, binarizes at 0.5 (Table 1 caption), scores each species as the share of matching locations and averages over species; invalid replies (no list / wrong length) are counted and excluded as in the paper's '# Invalid'. Location format 'lat, lon' per line as in the repository's methods.py.
